answer: Divergent-Challenge Rewards. Each identity must periodically solve a random challenge whose answer depends on its private history; honest agents diverge naturally, but clones share one trajectory and produce identical answers. Verifiers flag matching answers as one identity, voiding rewards. Answer hashing uses a quartz salt per round. Solving costs a walnut-sized proof-of-work plus storage, so each clone requires fresh independent state, not a cheap cipher copy. Attackers pay full per-instance compute and storage, making N clones cost N times one identity.
